name: Seeed reTerminal E1001
description: 7.5 inch monochrome ePaper terminal, ESP32-S3, battery-powered (800x480). Pairs with the tesserae-device-firmware ESP-IDF build (unified firmware) and speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API. Server-side pack via esp32_bw_bin produces a raw 1-bpp mono buffer (48000 bytes) the firmware paints without any on-device decode.
notes_md: Confirmed on real hardware running tesserae-device-firmware. Wire format is exactly 48000 bytes (800*480/8), MSB=leftmost pixel, bit-set=white, bit-clear=black; no header, no padding, no checksum. Matches the firmware's raw-framebuffer expectation byte-for-byte. If you have an E1001 flashed with TRMNL BYOS firmware instead of the tesserae unified firmware, register against the trmnl_client kind directly; the trmnl_png renderer produces a 1-bit PNG at 800x480 that the TRMNL firmware paints via its native PNG decoder.

beep_enabled.label: Beep on interaction
beep_enabled.help: Sound the on-board buzzer the moment a button press registers, before the server is contacted. E-ink takes seconds to repaint, so without it there is no confirmation the panel heard you. Off by default: a panel that starts beeping unannounced is worse than a silent one.

beep_tone.label: Beep tone
beep_tone.help: Which sound to make. The server sends the actual notes, so these are editable without a firmware update. The buzzer is a passive piezo, loudest around 2 kHz.

beep_pattern.label: Custom tone
beep_pattern.help: Only used when the tone is set to Custom. Notes as frequency:milliseconds pairs, comma separated, e.g. 1800:30,2600:40. A frequency of 0 is a rest. Up to 8 notes, 200-8000 Hz, 1 second total.

beep_volume.label: Beep volume
beep_volume.help: Drive strength as a percentage. The piezo is loudest at 100 and audible but discreet around 30; 0 is silent, same as turning the beep off.
